findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Hot dogs on the hot dog rollers are observed with internal temperatures of 78F-84F. Ambient air temperature is observed as 74F by the same thermometer. The PIC was unaware of any warming that had taken place yet today. Investigation showed that an employee had partially warmed the items recently and then turned off the equipment. Education was conducted in relation to warming and hot holding. The hot dogs were discarded at noon as that was the safest estimate for a four hour pathogen growth curve. Ensure that all hot foods are maintained above 135F at all times.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Diced tomatoes in the cooler section of the refrigerator are observed with internal temperatures of 47F. Investigation showed that the dial regulating the cooler temperature has been bumped. The dial was re-adjusted. The tomatoes were the only TCS item observed below acceptable limits and were discarded during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

Cleaners, motor oil, lighter fluid and other chemicals are observed on shelves over foods in the retail section of the facility. This situation was shown and discussed with he PIC during this inspection. The noted items were moved to correct the immediate violation. A re-arranging of the shelves is going to be conducted by the PIC moving forward to ensure that this is not a concern in the future. Ensure that all chemicals not intended for foods or food contact surfaces are stored so that potential contamination of these surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS.

During this inspection the probe capable of measuring the full range of food temperatures would not turn on. The battery was changed and multiple attempts made to turn it on to no avail. An employee was sent to the store and acquired a new probe thermometer during this inspection to correct the violation. The PIC was instructed to ensure that a functional probe thermometer is available at the facility at all times.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location.

The tongs used for handling hot dogs are observed in a container that also contains a brush and has food debris in the bottom. The location was discussed and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all in-use food contact surfaces are protected from contamination between uses.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips are available that are intended for use with a CL based solution. The only sanitizer currently available in the facility is quat based. The difference was discussed and the PIC instructed to acquire test strips that are intended for use with the available sanitizer. An employee was sent to acquire a new set of strips the match their available sanitizer. They returned prior to the inspector leaving to correct the violation with bleach.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared for use in the facility. Foods have started to be preparation at this time. The situation was discussed with the PIC and a bucket made during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer is ready for use at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.
